recommendations: HEADLINE: Zero booked calls across 2098 sends and ~$285 in Places spend (Hunter not included). The pipeline is producing replies (18 lifetime) but no replies have converted to booked calls. This is the cost-cut decision point: either the ICP is wrong, the email copy isn't earning the click-through to Calendly, or Calendly itself is dropping interest. Pull a sample of the 18 replies and read them in voice — what's the most common reason they engaged but didn't book?

Bounce rate of 7.7% is borderline (target: under 5%). Garage door, electrician, plumber, and handyman trades show higher bounce rates (9-12%) — Hunter is feeding more stale addresses for these verticals. Tighten Hunter confidence threshold for high-bounce trades or drop them until the data is cleaner.

Reply rate is 0.86% — well under typical cold-outreach benchmarks (2-5% for B2B services). Two interpretations: (a) Email #1 isn't compelling — the subject line or first sentence isn't earning the open and the read; (b) the audit/heatmap hook isn't landing for trades where GBP is less central to lead-gen. Either way, the current copy is the primary lever. Rewrite Email #1, A/B subject lines on the next 200 sends, measure delta.

Email #3 has fired 1212 times. 1203 rows currently sit in FOLLOW-UP-2 status — that's the universe Email #3 was supposed to convert, and only 18 replies have surfaced across the entire campaign (most likely on E1 or E2). The third touch isn't earning its slot. Two options: kill Email #3 entirely (saves Hunter cost on verifying still-valid sends, reduces sender-reputation drag from low-engagement messages), OR rewrite as a hard-breakup with one concrete ask and a specific deadline. Default recommendation: kill it for the next 2 weeks, measure if reply rate on E1+E2 holds.

Cut bottom yielders: roofer, plumber, hvac. These three trades absorbed 322 sends with zero replies between them. They're consuming Hunter credits, Places API spend, and sender-reputation capacity that would convert better in higher-yield verticals. Drop them from rotation immediately.

Concentrate spend on top performers: pest control, tree service, electrician. These are the only trades showing reply rates near or above the 2% benchmark. Increase rotation weight for these verticals; expand city coverage in them before adding any new trade. Pest control's small sample (24 sends) needs more volume to confirm the signal.

Cost-per-reply is ~$15.85 on Places spend alone. Cost-per-booked is undefined (zero booked). Adding Hunter subscription (Starter plan ~$49/mo) plus operator time, true cost-per-booked is currently infinite. Until a single booked call hits, the program is net cost — this is the cost-cut signal. Either accept a 4-6 week burn-while-you-fix-copy window, or pause sends and rewrite before spending more.
